brief.headline: Black Friday is full of fake deals, so today we show the one thing nobody else will: a real room at its real price.
brief.summary: Today is Black Friday. UK coverage is full of warnings about fake deals, which gives a brand with visible, VAT-included prices an easy contrast that people will comment on. Christmas formats are climbing on Reels: the "Dear Santa" letter, and the brand-new "my coffee sounded weird" sound gag, which we can turn into a brass-and-water moment. On Pinterest and in home magazines, the "living room treatment" (lived-in bathrooms with furniture vanities, art and mixed metals) and "brassware as jewellery" are the strongest aesthetics this week, and both match our warm stone, walnut and gold look. Lead today with a Guess the Price Reel and a lived-in bathroom carousel. Support them with Pinterest collages and 2:3 pins that link to the studio, and put a licensed instrumental on every carousel so it can show in the Reels tab.

trends.name: Black Friday counter-programming: priced, not discounted
trends.what_it_is: Black Friday is today (27 November) and the weekend runs to Cyber Monday on 30 November. UK coverage is dominated by fake-deal warnings and sales that started in October.
trends.why_now: It peaks today and fades after Monday 30 November. NationalWorld, Shopappy and Which? are all running Black Friday and fake-deal coverage this week.
trends.how_we_use_it: No discount. We make the contrast instead: 'The only thing we're taking off is the guesswork.' Show a real room priced to the pound with VAT included, and make a Guess the Price quiz of it so people comment.

trends.name: The living room treatment (lived-in bathrooms)
trends.what_it_is: Bathrooms that feel like real rooms: furniture-style vanities, upholstered stools, art, rugs, pendants and wall lights instead of spotlights, mixed metals and warm stone.
trends.why_now: Homes & Gardens published 'the living room treatment' on 23 November 2026. Its 2027 bathroom trends piece (23 October 2026) leads with 'bathrooms that feel like actual rooms'.
trends.how_we_use_it: Make a save-led carousel and a set of 2:3 pins built around the Onsen Light Walnut vanity (£950) and the Artize stone basin (£1,243). Add one practical slide on which soft pieces survive humidity.

trends.name: Dear Santa wishlist
trends.what_it_is: On-screen text written as a letter to Santa over clips of the things on the wishlist.
trends.why_now: Later logged it on 20 November 2026. SocialPilot ranks its usual sound among the top audios for 17 to 25 November, and Christmas audio is climbing on every tracker.
trends.how_we_use_it: Write 'Dear Santa, my bathroom is 2.1 m by 1.7 m...', with each wish cutting to a studio render of that piece and its VAT-included price. It works for the small-space audience and is easy to send to whoever is buying the present.

trends.name: 'My coffee sounded weird this morning' (an object starts a song)
trends.what_it_is: Stirring a coffee starts a festive song and taking the spoon out stops it. It is a sound gag built on original audio.
trends.why_now: Later logged it today, 27 November 2026. It is brand new, so whoever posts first gets the most from it.
trends.how_we_use_it: 'My bath sounded different this morning.' Turning on the Jaquar floor-mounted bath mixer (£2,251) brings in a warm instrumental. Turning it off leaves silence and steam. Film it as a moody brass-and-water close-up.

trends.name: Brassware as jewellery and mixed metals
trends.what_it_is: Taps and hardware treated as decoration: cross handles, backplates, antique-style fittings, and polished nickel deliberately mixed with aged brass.
trends.why_now: Homes & Gardens' 2027 trends piece (23 October 2026) quotes a designer calling them 'almost like jewelry for a bathroom'. Mixed metals come up again in its 23 November piece.
trends.how_we_use_it: Use 'One Piece, Three Rooms': one Jaquar mixer styled into three palettes, shot as slow macro close-ups, posted as a carousel and pinned slide by slide to a 'Brassware as jewellery' board.

trends.name: Carousels with music in the Reels tab, plus Replace Audio
trends.what_it_is: Carousels with music are showing in the Reels tab again, so they can reach non-followers. Audio on a published carousel can now be swapped without losing engagement, and likes can be seen per slide.
trends.why_now: SocialBee (updated 23 November 2026) and Ethical SMM (November 2026) both report it. Edits has built carousels since 7 October 2026. These are secondary sources, so check them against @creators.
trends.how_we_use_it: Every carousel today goes out with a licensed instrumental from the business account's library. Use per-slide likes to learn which palette or room wins.

trends.name: 'Don't let a ___ see this' (forbidden-content hook)
trends.what_it_is: On-screen text suggests the viewer is seeing something they shouldn't. It reliably starts arguments in the comments.
trends.why_now: Virlo marks it Rising in the week to 27 November 2026, with top Reels at 3.1M, 1M and 993K views.
trends.how_we_use_it: 'Don't let a minimalist see this' over a layered studio render with patterned tile, mixed metals and a furniture vanity. Keep the pacing slow and the grade calm, and never use a real customer's room.

trends.name: Guest-ready bathroom for Christmas hosting
trends.what_it_is: Seasonal 'get the bathroom ready for Christmas guests' content: layered lighting, soft towels, a light scent, spare toiletries.
trends.why_now: Ideal Home, Woman & Home and Dowsing & Reynolds are running guest-ready guides now. Seasonal searching peaks up to 24 December.

ideas.title: Black Friday quiz: what does this room cost?
ideas.trend: Black Friday counter-programming: priced, not discounted
ideas.hook: Black Friday quiz: guess what this whole room costs.
ideas.concept: Today's UK feeds are full of 'was' prices and fake-deal warnings. This Reel answers them with one real room at one real price. Slow, controlled pans across the website's six-piece shop-the-look room ask viewers to pause and comment their guess. The last frame reveals £11,533.84, VAT included and priced to the pound, with 'Nothing's off. Everything's priced.' and an invitation to set their own budget in the free 3D studio.
ideas.why_it_works: Black Friday peaks today. NationalWorld, Shopappy and Which? are all running fake-deal and early-sale warnings, so a brand showing an exact price with VAT included stands out without criticising anyone. A guessing game gets comments from people who don't follow us. A 'send this to the person you're renovating with' line gets sends, and sends per reach is still Instagram's strongest signal for reaching non-followers (Ethical SMM, November 2026). Holding the answer until the end gets rewatches and more watch time. Lightreel (14 to 21 Nov) found that simple bathroom moments with one strong line on screen beat busy seasonal edits, so the cut is text-led and calm. It is also a ready-made episode of the Guess the Price series, so the format can run again after the weekend.

reel.audio: A licensed instrumental from Meta's Reels library, picked inside the business account. Go for slow piano or soft, warm downtempo at about 80 to 90 BPM. Original audio also works. Add one soft chime or brass 'tick' on the price reveal at 0:12. Don't use commercial Christmas or Black Friday tracks (for example Wham!'s 'Last Christmas') unless they show as cleared in the business account's library. I haven't verified any Black Friday sound as trending, so don't name one.

reel.edit_notes: Use Cormorant Garamond for the headline text and Inter for small lines, in cream on footage and gold for the price only. Keep every move slow and controlled with soft cross-dissolves. No hard cuts on the beat, no red, no countdown timers, no flashing or 'SALE' styling. Keep the cover frame as the hook text over the wide room and keep the price off the cover and out of the caption's first lines so the reveal isn't spoiled. Add a small 'Designed in our 3D studio' tag in the corner of the render shots so they read clearly as designs. Let the end frame hold so the loop restarts on the hook, which helps rewatches.

ideas.title: 5 ways to make your bathroom feel like a room, not a utility
ideas.hook: Your bathroom is a room. Stop designing it like a utility.
ideas.concept: An 8-slide carousel that is easy to save. It shows the 'living room treatment' five ways: a vanity that looks like furniture, a stone counter-top basin, one piece of art, wall lights in place of a grid of spotlights, and soft pieces that can live with steam. Two hero pieces carry real, VAT-included prices, and one practical slide on humidity gives it Know Before You Renovate credibility. It posts with a licensed instrumental so it can show in the Reels tab, and each slide is cut down into its own 2:3 Pinterest pin that links to the studio.
ideas.why_it_works: Homes & Gardens ran 'the living room treatment' on 23 Nov 2026 and led its 2027 bathroom trends piece (23 Oct) with 'bathrooms that feel like actual rooms'. So this rides an aesthetic with editorial momentum this week, and it fits our warm stone, walnut and gold look (brand fit 92 in the dossier). SocialBee (23 Nov) and Ethical SMM (Nov 2026) report that carousels with music are being shown in the Reels tab again, which gives a save-led format a route to non-followers. Per-slide likes will show which of the five ideas lands, and that feeds the next post. On Pinterest, numbered text-on-image guides and 2:3 statics suit the inspiration savers who plan months ahead. The dossier also notes a content gap: Victorian Plumbing lost organic visibility because its informational content was thin. The humidity slide is what makes this more than a moodboard.

slides.headline: 3. Hang one piece of art
slides.body: One framed print at eye level, away from the shower. It is the quickest way to tell a room it is not a utility.
slides.visual: Render or styled photo: a simple framed print under glass on a warm limewash or panelled wall above a towel rail. Navy-teal #174A5C text panel on the left third.

slides.headline: 4. Swap the spotlight grid for wall lights
slides.body: Wall lights either side of the mirror and a pendant over the bath, kept well clear of the water. Antique brass lights with brushed nickel taps: mixing metals is part of the look. Bathroom lights follow zones and IP ratings, so your electrician confirms what can go where.
slides.visual: Dusk render of two warm wall lights framing a mirror, with a soft pendant glow beyond. Deep navy-teal #081C26 shadows and gold #E4C99B highlights. Text in cream.

slides.headline: 5. Add soft pieces that can take the steam
slides.body: Yes: prints framed behind glass, a cotton rug you can wash, a teak or sealed-wood stool, a performance-fabric seat kept out of the splash zone. Think twice: unframed paper, velvet beside the shower, untreated wood. Whatever you choose, a good extractor fan does the heavy lifting.

The line 'send this to whoever's buying your present' is built for sends, and the dossier names sends per reach as Instagram's strongest signal for reaching non-followers. The exact measurements speak straight to the small-space and en-suite audience, and they show the studio's drag-to-size feature without explaining it. Lightreel (14 to 21 Nov) found that simple bathroom moments with one strong line beat busy seasonal edits, so this is text-led, slow and calm. Real prices on each wish set us apart in a week full of fake-deal warnings.

# Research dossier: Bespoke Bathroom UK, brand and viral reach
**Date:** Friday 27 November 2026 (Black Friday). **Window:** today to about 8 December 2026. **Platforms:** Instagram and Pinterest (Pinterest Lab on).

**How sure I am:** No platform-owned trend data could be read today. Pinterest Predicts 2027 isn't published until 8 December, and the Pinterest Trends tool needs a login. The Instagram trend and audio rankings come from third-party trackers (Later, Virlo, SocialPilot, CreatorDB, Lightreel), and they don't agree with each other. Check every sound in the Reels audio library on the business account before posting.

---

## Trends

### 1. "Dear Santa" wishlist
- **Platforms:** Instagram Reels (also works as a story frame and a Pinterest idea pin)
- **Kind:** Seasonal text-led format
- **What it is:** On-screen text written as a letter ("Dear Santa, I'm a size...") over clips of the wished-for things. Later logged it on 20 November with Wham!'s "Last Christmas (Instrumental)".
- **Momentum:** Later, 20 Nov 2026. SocialPilot ranks "Last Christmas" in its top audios for 17 to 25 Nov. Christmas audio is climbing on every tracker.
- **How we use it:** "Dear Santa, my bathroom is 2.1 m by 1.7 m. I'd like a walk-in shower, a wall-hung vanity and to stop showering under a tile I hate." Each line cuts to a studio render of that piece with its price (VAT included). The last frame says "Santa's running late. The studio isn't. Design yours free." This fits the small-space audience, sharing is built in ("send this to whoever's buying your present"), and the measurements make it exact.
- **Audio:** Don't use the Wham! track unless it shows as cleared in the business account's library. Use a licensed festive instrumental or original audio.
- **Brand fit:** 85. **Momentum:** Rising. **Lifespan:** About 3 to 4 weeks, to Christmas.
- **Sources:** [Later](https://later.com/blog/instagram-reels-trends/), [SocialPilot](https://www.socialpilot.co/blog/instagram-reels-trends)

### 2. "I feel like I haven't done much this year" (year in review)
- **Platforms:** Instagram Reels and carousels
- **Kind:** End-of-year format
- **What it is:** An opening line saying you haven't done much, then clips labelled month by month that prove otherwise. Later logged it on 20 November with Harry Styles' "Coming Up Roses". SocialPilot says that sound went from 49K to 116K Reels in under three weeks.
- **Momentum:** Later, 20 Nov 2026. SocialPilot, 17 to 25 Nov 2026.
- **How we use it:** "We feel like we haven't done much this year." Then "January: [ADD: real room]", "March: [ADD]"... Each month is a screen-to-room cut or a studio render. Only use rooms that are real and that customers have given permission for. If there aren't 12, do "six rooms we designed this year". Don't invent counts. A carousel version with one month per slide gets saves and makes a good pinned post for December.
- **Audio:** Use original audio or a licensed piano track.
- **Brand fit:** 80. **Momentum:** Rising, peaking through December. **Lifespan:** To early January.
- **Sources:** [Later](https://later.com/blog/instagram-reels-trends/), [SocialPilot](https://www.socialpilot.co/blog/instagram-reels-trends)

### 3. "My coffee sounded weird this morning" (an object starts a song)
- **Platforms:** Instagram Reels
- **Kind:** Sound gag and transition
- **What it is:** Stirring coffee starts a holiday song. Taking the spoon out stops it. Later logged it on 27 November (today) on original audio.
- **Momentum:** Later, 27 Nov 2026. It's brand new.
- **How we use it:** "My bath sounded different this morning." Turn on the Jaquar floor-mounted bath mixer (£2,251), and a slow, warm instrumental rises with the water. Turn it off and there's silence and steam. It's a moody close-up of brass and water in our usual palette, and it's a "quiet mornings" moment you can see. Close on the Artize Tiaara freestanding bath (£6,626) and "See it in your room first. Free 3D design."
- **Audio:** Original audio or a licensed library track only. Real water sound works well as the "before".
- **Brand fit:** 82. **Momentum:** New. **Lifespan:** 1 to 3 weeks, so film this weekend.
- **Sources:** [Later](https://later.com/blog/instagram-reels-trends/)

### 4. "Don't let a ___ see this" (forbidden-content hook)
- **Platforms:** Instagram Reels
- **Kind:** Text hook meme
- **What it is:** On-screen text hints the viewer is seeing something they shouldn't. Virlo marks it Rising in the week to 27 November, with top Reels at 3.1M, 1M and 993K views.
- **Momentum:** Virlo, data as of 27 Nov 2026.
- **How we use it:** "Don't let a minimalist see this." Show a layered room with patterned tile, mixed metals and a furniture vanity, which ties into trends 6 and 7. Another version is "Don't let your fitter see this price", showing a full room priced to the pound inside budget. People will argue in the comments, and that's what we want. Keep the tone affectionate and never mock a customer's home.
- **Audio:** Virlo's tracked sound ("PHANTOM LIQUID DESIRE") isn't confirmed as cleared. Use original audio.
- **Brand fit:** 68. It's playful, so the grading and pacing need to stay calm. **Momentum:** Rising. **Lifespan:** About 2 weeks.
- **Sources:** [Virlo Instagram trends](https://virlo.ai/instagram-trends)

### 5. Black Friday counter-programming: "Nothing's off. Everything's priced."
- **Platforms:** Instagram (Reel, stories, carousel), Pinterest
- **Kind:** Dated cultural moment
- **What it is:** Black Friday is today, 27 November, and the weekend runs to Cyber Monday on 30 November. UK coverage is full of fake-deal warnings and retailers' sales running from October to 1 December.

Then show a £15,000 studio room priced to the pound with VAT included, and the fact that the design costs nothing and needs no sign-up. A "Guess the Price" Reel works this weekend: "Black Friday quiz: what does this room cost?" with the real six-piece shop-the-look total of £11,533.84. People will comment their guesses, which drives reach to non-followers.
- **Brand fit:** 88. **Momentum:** Peak today. **Lifespan:** 4 days.
- **Sources:** [NationalWorld](https://www.nationalworld.com/recommended/black-friday-2026-9268295), [Shopappy on fake deals](https://shopappy.com/consumer-trends/discount-value/black-friday-2026-uk-early-sales-fake-deals), [Which?](https://www.which.co.uk/news/black-friday/)

- **Kind:** Aesthetic

Designers suggest mixed metals (antique brass wall lights with brushed nickel taps), warm stone and paneling.

- **How we use it:** A carousel called "5 ways to make your bathroom feel like a room, not a utility". Use the Onsen Vanity Unit 2D W.120 in Light Walnut (£950) as the furniture-style piece and the Artize stone counter-top basin (£1,243), and add a practical slide on what survives humidity (that's our "Know before you renovate" credibility). Pin each slide on its own as a 2:3 static pin.
- **Brand fit:** 92, because it matches warm stone, walnut and gold. **Momentum:** Rising, with editorial coverage this week. **Lifespan:** Months, as a 2027 theme.
- **Sources:** [Homes & Gardens, lived-in bathroom](https://www.homesandgardens.com/decor/bathrooms/lived-in-bathroom-trend), [Homes & Gardens UK, 2027 trends](https://www.homesandgardens.com/uk/decor/bathrooms/bathroom-trends-2027)

### 7. "Jewellery for the bathroom": decorative brassware and mixed metals
- **Platforms:** Instagram Reels (macro close-ups), Pinterest
- **Kind:** Aesthetic and product moment
- **What it is:** Taps and hardware treated as decoration: cross handles, backplates, antique-style fittings, polished nickel deliberately mixed with aged brass. A designer quoted by Homes & Gardens called them "almost like jewelry for a bathroom".

## Pinterest signals

**Where the data stands.** There's no current Pinterest search-growth data for bathrooms in public. Pinterest Predicts 2027 arrives on 8 December. Pinterest has said its predictions were 88% accurate over the past six years. Its newsroom post of 17 November confirms the date and names its first "Creators to Watch for 2027", including UK creators. The 2026 Predicts home themes are still being saved: Neo Deco (Art Deco revival), "afrobohemian" decor, opalescent finishes and circus stripes. Of those, only Neo Deco really suits us. Pinterest's Spring 2026 report framed home projects as "micro-renovations", which supports content about upgrading one piece at a time.

**Aesthetics being saved and written about (editorial evidence from Oct to Nov 2026):**
- Lived-in bathrooms, or the "living room treatment": furniture vanities, upholstered stools, art, pendants
- Warm, earthy palettes replacing all-white spa rooms: espresso and chocolate, warm stone, dark wood
- Bolder material mixes: espresso pill tiles with natural stone, glossy small tiles against large slabs
- Brassware as jewellery: mixed nickel and aged brass, cross handles, backplates
- Tile as a focal point: zellige, herringbone floors, long thin tiles, tiled panels that look like millwork
- Reeded glass replacing frosted screens, and fabric curtains replacing glass over baths
- Built-in baths coming back
- "Texture drenching" and "lightscaping" (layered lighting)
- Wet rooms that look unified
- Green paint: Soulful Sage and Celery
- On Pinterest boards, "zen bathroom" and "natural spa" persist. This comes from a secondary source, so treat it with caution.

**Pin formats:**
- **Collages:** Pinterest's own August 2026 beauty analysis found video pins got about 1.2x the saves of image pins, collages came close behind, and collages drove the most clicks. Pinterest says the format is especially popular with Gen Z, and each cutout can link to a product. This is ideal for "shop the look" with each piece tagged and priced.
- **Static 2:3 pins** with a clear focal point and keyword-led titles. Pinterest's guidance is to open video pins on the result.
- **Multi-slide or carousel pins:** One vendor study (GenSumo, March 2026) says they have the best save rate, but its own figures contradict each other. Test them rather than assume.

## What is working for comparable brands

I found little published evidence of specific UK bathroom-brand posts going viral this month. These are the defensible signals:
- **Dulux "one room, four ways"** with its 2027 colour. One room shown in several versions is the house format for colour moments. That supports "Spanish to Japanese" and "One Piece, Three Rooms".
- **Victorian Plumbing** has the most brand demand among UK bathroom retailers, but its organic search visibility more than halved in the year to May 2026. Salience blames thin informational content, while Big Bathroom Shop wins on inspiration guides. That leaves room for "Know Before You Renovate" on YouTube and Pinterest.
- **Pearler**, an investing app, ran a bathroom-set campaign in November 2026. Its creator skit ("Toilet cubicle financial planning") passed 1M Instagram views, and sign-ups rose 18% that week. Bathroom-as-setting humour still travels. That supports "The Bath Arrived Three Weeks Before the Taps".

## Lead-gen angles

1. **Black Friday Guess the Price** (today to Monday). Comments guess the total, then reveal £11,533.84 priced to the pound. The CTA is "Set your own budget, free. Design your bathroom in 3D."
2. **Dear Santa, my bathroom is...** Followers comment their room size. Reply with "Comment DESIGN and we'll send the studio link", and start a "Your Bathroom, Redesigned" thread from the replies.
3. **"Design it over Christmas"**. Pitch the studio as a calm job for the Christmas lull, so homeowners start January with a priced design and a designer's stock check.
4. **Pantone reactive render** (3 Dec). "Want it in your room? Upload a photo, free."
5. **Pinterest collage "shop the look" pins** linking to products and the studio. They suit savers months before renovating.
6. **Comment-to-DM planning checklist** ([PLAN] lead magnet) attached to the living-room-treatment and guest-ready carousels.
7. **Cost guide teaser** ([COST] magnet). Use studio budget tiers from £1,000 to £100,000 as a January anchor, and pin it now.

## Watch-outs

- **Music licensing:** Wham!'s "Last Christmas", "Coming Up Roses", Kanye West's "Runaway", the GTA VI tracks and Tate McRae's "Housewife" are commercial. Business accounts usually can't use them. Use original audio, voiceover or Meta's licensed library, and check inside the business account. Replace Audio lets you upgrade later.
- **Tracker reliability:** The audio and trend rankings from Virlo, Later, SocialPilot and CreatorDB don't agree. Treat them as signals and check in-app before filming.
- **Black Friday tone:** No "deals", "% off", countdowns or urgency. That breaks the voice and the "no cheap discount language" rule. The contrast idea only works if it stays calm.
- **Pantone leak:** "Aqua Splash" is unconfirmed. Don't publish it as fact before 3 December.
- **Pinterest Predicts 2027:** It doesn't exist until 8 December. Don't quote 2027 Pinterest trend names or percentages until then.
- **Claims:**
  - The year-in-review and "one team" posts need real rooms, real counts and written permission. Leave [ADD] placeholders until then.
  - No review quotes until real ones exist.
  - Don't promise fitting before Christmas unless lead times are confirmed.
- **Prices:** Use the Brand Brain figures with VAT included: Jaquar mixer £2,251, Tiaara bath £6,626, Onsen vanity £950, Artize basin £1,243, Dell mirror £263.84, look total £11,533.84.
- **Consent:** No customers' homes or faces without written permission. "Don't let a ___ see this" must never use or mock a real customer's room.
- **AI content:** If renders or AI scenes include people, the "AI-generated" labelling rules apply. Keep studio renders clearly framed as designs.
- **Originality:** Rebuild every trend with our own footage. Lightly edited reposts of other creators lose reach.
